title: What to watch at today's open
text: Stocks ended Monday higher. The S&P 500 fund SPY closed at $765.37, up 0.7%, and the Nasdaq 100 fund QQQ closed at $712.20, up 1.1%. Today, watch how stocks start after that gain, because the big reports are close. The Federal Reserve meets today and tomorrow, with its decision on Wednesday, October 28. Alphabet and Microsoft report that day, and Amazon reports Thursday. Big news can move prices fast. This is for learning, not advice.

title: Fed meeting this week
text: The Federal Reserve, the group that sets the main interest rate, meets October 27 and 28, and shares its decision on Wednesday afternoon. Interest rates are the price of borrowing money, so they affect many stocks at once. Growth companies like the AI names often react the most. The decision lands on the same day as Alphabet and Microsoft earnings, so Wednesday may be a bumpy day.

title: Lockheed Martin is close to its analyst target
text: Lockheed Martin closed at $635.20, up 5.1%, a big move for a stock with a beta of only 0.10. Beta tells us how much a stock usually moves compared with the whole market, and a low beta means it normally moves less. The price is now just 0.5% below the average analyst target of $638.22. A target is only an opinion, not a promise, and we could not confirm what caused the jump.

title: Chip stocks rally, but Vertiv is still far from its high
text: AMD rose 2.8% to $531.28, NVIDIA rose 2.4% to $216.00, Broadcom rose 2.3% and Vertiv rose 2.8%. Even so, Vertiv is still 47.4% below its 52 week high, and AMD has a risk score of 7.4 out of 10 because its price swings are big. One good day does not tell us what comes next.

title: Lesson 24: What is a profit margin?
text: A profit margin tells us how many cents a company keeps from each dollar it sells. Say a lemonade stand sells $100 of lemonade and, after paying for lemons, cups and helpers, keeps $20. Its profit margin is 20%. A higher margin means the company keeps more of each sale. NVIDIA keeps about 64 cents of each dollar, while Amazon keeps about 17 cents, because selling and shipping products costs a lot. A lower margin is not always bad, since it depends on the kind of business. Compare companies that do similar things. This is for learning, not advice to buy or sell anything.

title: What this board covers
text: All 17 stocks and funds have prices from Monday's close, since the market has not opened yet today. Analyst price targets came through for NVDA, TSM, AMD, GOOGL, AMZN, MSFT, META, GE and LMT.
